overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated FACTVERSE performance data reveals that high-concept space and astrophysics videos—specifically featuring extreme planetary conditions, 'What If' scenarios, and planetary oddities—are dominating engagement and velocity. Videos like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year', 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' significantly outperform general psychological or biology facts in views, likes-per-view, and sustained momentum.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) show exceptional engagement compared to older psychology or standard animal facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on surreal astronomical 'What If' scenarios that force the viewer to visualize impossible physics.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring planetary anomalies like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,031 views, 36 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views) capture immediate curiosity and high like-to-view ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Continue utilizing high-contrast cosmic anomalies with specific, mind-boggling adjectives (darker, rains, heavier, colder).

weak_patterns.pattern: Low-Engagement Psychological Tricks & Common Biology Facts
weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) show very weak traction and poor audience pull relative to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological hacks and everyday animal trivia unless paired with a massive, counter-intuitive evolutionary mystery.
